lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Decision Analysis and Expected Value Capstone
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: empirical probability distributions from data

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read the example first. You are not expected to know this yet.

items.prompt: Costs $5, pays $40 with probability 1/10. Expected value?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Try each one. If you get stuck, write what you do know and move on.

items.prompt: An insurer charges a premium of $9 and pays out $540 with probability 1/90. Find the insurer's expected profit per policy.
Option A has expected payoff $22 and Option B has expected payoff $30. On expected value alone, which should be chosen, and what does this criterion ignore?
choices: Option B; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Neither; expected value cannot compare two options.
Option A; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Option B; expected value already accounts for risk, so nothing is ignored.

items.prompt: Assess whether this is a fair decision mechanism: choosing between three people by rolling a standard die, assigning two faces to each.
choices: Not fair; the three probabilities are 3/6, 2/6, and 1/6, which are unequal.
Fair; each person receives probability 2/6 = 1/3, so the assignment is equal.
Fair; each person has probability 1/2, and the mechanism gives neither an advantage.
Fair, because any random device produces a fair decision.

items.prompt: A game costs $14 to play. It pays $90 with probability 1/5 and nothing otherwise. Find the expected value to the player, and say whether the game is fair.
choices: $4; the game is favourable to the player
$-14; the game is unfavourable to the player
$18; the game is favourable to the player
$76; the game is favourable to the player

items.prompt: An insurer charges a premium of $14 and pays out $736 with probability 1/92. Find the insurer's expected profit per policy.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Show what you can do so far. This sets the starting point, not a grade.

items.prompt: Option A has expected payoff $21 and Option B has expected payoff $10. On expected value alone, which should be chosen, and what does this criterion ignore?
choices: Option B; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Option A; expected value ignores the spread of outcomes and the decider's tolerance for risk.
Neither; expected value cannot compare two options.
Option A; expected value already accounts for risk, so nothing is ignored.

items.prompt: Assess whether this is a fair decision mechanism: choosing between two people using a single fair coin flip.
choices: Not fair; the three probabilities are 3/6, 2/6, and 1/6, which are unequal.
Fair, because any random device produces a fair decision.
Fair; each person has probability 1/2, and the mechanism gives neither an advantage.
Fair; each person receives probability 2/6 = 1/3, so the assignment is equal.
